query: Where Things Are Bram reads the castle to you off his ledger. "Job Board, by the stairs: work and wages. Library: revision tables before every exam. Infirmary, on the Alchemy floor: Sister Amaranth, for when you break something, yourself included. The village, down the hill: robes and wands on market day, tea at Mabel's, tonics at Pell's." He snaps the ledger shut. "Questions? No. Good." "No questions." "Excellent," says Bram, and means it. He leaves you at the foot of the stairs with a map in your head and a strong sense of having been processed. Ask what he left out He looks pained. "The Gilded Newt, in the village, after dark: supper, cider and people you shouldn't be seen with. The Lakeshore, for thinking. That's all." He writes something in the ledger. It might be your name.
